# Favour at Flamong — Policy.ng frontend engineering

**Position:** Frontend Developer Intern at Flamong.  
**Employment period:** May 2026–Present, confirmed on 10 November 2026.  
**Product:** [Policy.ng](https://policy.ng/)  
**Role:** Frontend engineering for the public website and administrative dashboard.

## Product and responsibility

Policy.ng helps visitors find and understand public policies and information about public officials. It also includes civic content and AI-assisted policy questions, with administrative features for managing the information and interactions on the site.

Favour is the sole frontend engineer on the product. He builds and maintains the public-facing pages and authenticated administration tools using React and TypeScript. His work includes policy search and detail views, public-official directories, AI-assisted question interfaces, comments and administrative replies, moderation, content editing, and subscriber management.

His responsibility at Policy.ng is the frontend, including the integration of its AI-assisted question interface. The product's backend and underlying AI services are separate from that frontend responsibility.

## Frontend integration and workflows

Favour integrates the frontend with the backend using TanStack Query. When an API response differs from what a screen expects, or a new workflow needs an additional endpoint, he works with the backend engineer to resolve it. He has adapted the comments experience to support nested administrative replies and updated the affected UI states.

Favour's Policy.ng frontend work includes form validation with React Hook Form and Zod, authenticated navigation, role and permission checks, state updates after administrative actions, and handling failures without losing the user's work.

## Administration, testing, and collaboration

The administrative side also requires permission checks, forms that reject invalid data, protection against duplicate submissions, warnings for unsaved edits, and refreshed information after updates. Favour has added automated coverage for selected workflows with Vitest and Playwright. He collaborates with the product manager, backend engineer, mobile engineer, and company leadership during development and release.

# BlockScan — Sepolia blockchain explorer

**Type:** Independent frontend project  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/sepolia-blockexplorer  
**Application:** https://blockscan-seven.vercel.app/  
**Stack:** React, JavaScript, React Router, React Testing Library, Alchemy SDK/RPC, Vercel.

## Overview

BlockScan is a blockchain explorer for Ethereum Sepolia. It lets users inspect blocks, transactions, wallet addresses, account activity, and NFT metadata.

## Search and live-data implementation

Favour built a global search feature that distinguishes block numbers, transaction hashes, and wallet addresses and opens the appropriate result. The live-block feed checks for new data while preventing overlapping requests and duplicate results. It preserves the existing results if a refresh fails and avoids unnecessary polling when the page is not visible.

BlockScan's live-block feed also avoids updates that overwrite valid information.

## Navigation, watchlist, and credential handling

For BlockScan, Favour also built a persistent watchlist, keyboard-accessible search, route-level code splitting, and Vercel API proxies that keep Alchemy credentials out of the browser bundle.

The credentials described here are Alchemy provider API credentials, not
database credentials. This documents a credential-exposure control, not
proof that the application prevents every form of unauthorized access.

# Monierave — Full-stack banking simulation

**Type:** Independent full-stack project  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/monierave  
**Application:** https://monierave.favourututu.com/  
**Stack:** Go, Gin, PostgreSQL, SQLC, pgx, Redis, Asynq, Next.js, React, TypeScript, TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod, Docker.

## Overview and contribution

Monierave is a banking simulation through which Favour explored the backend and frontend engineering of financial transactions. He built account registration and verification, authentication, account management, beneficiaries, transfers, transaction history, statements, and profile and security features.

Monierave is a portfolio banking simulation, not a licensed bank or a service for handling customers' real money.

## Transfer integrity and concurrency

A transfer in Monierave is recorded through an append-only double-entry ledger. PostgreSQL transactions keep related database changes together, row-level locking deals with concurrent account operations, and idempotency keys help prevent the same request from creating duplicate transfers. Business rules are enforced by the backend.

Monierave's transactional outbox connects durable database changes to asynchronous processing. Workers can retry tasks without treating the database and the job queue as a single transaction.

These mechanisms have distinct roles: idempotency keys address repeated
transfer requests; transactions keep related writes atomic; row locks
coordinate concurrent account operations; the outbox records background
work durably. This is a description of the implementation's design, not an
independently verified guarantee of exactly-once transfers or job delivery.

## Background processing and security

Background work uses a transactional outbox. PostgreSQL holds the durable record of work to be performed, while Redis and Asynq support processing and retries. The system also includes rotating refresh tokens, revocable sessions, audit records, and reconciliation-related checks.

These Monierave features were built into a banking simulation and demonstrate the backend design problems Favour addressed in its implementation.

For notification failures after a committed transfer, the outbox permits
background retry without making successful notification delivery a
condition of that already committed transfer. The documented material does
not specify an email retry limit or guarantee eventual delivery. It does
not establish retries forever or until successful.

## Frontend and testing

On the frontend, Favour used TanStack Query to manage server data and React Hook Form with Zod for form handling. He added backend, integration, and end-to-end tests, including tests for transfer behavior under concurrency.

## Limitations

Monierave is a portfolio banking simulation. It is not a licensed bank or a service for handling customers' real money.

No paying-customer count or current customer-usage measurement is recorded
in this knowledge base. That count is unknown; simulation status is not
evidence that the current paying-customer count is zero.

# BucketFlow — Stablecoin allocation application

**Type:** Independent blockchain application  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/bucketflow  
**Application:** https://bucketflow-tau.vercel.app/  
**Stack:** Next.js, React, TypeScript, TanStack Query, Solidity, wagmi, viem, Foundry.

## Overview and contribution

BucketFlow lets users set rules for splitting a USDC deposit among financial buckets, such as savings and other planned expenses. The allocation must account for the full deposit. Favour built the interface and connected it to a Solidity vault that applies the allocation and withdrawal rules.

BucketFlow's documented application uses Ethereum Sepolia, a test network. It is a demonstration of on-chain allocation logic, not a regulated savings product.

## Wallet and transaction implementation

BucketFlow handles wallet connection, token spending approvals, deposits, transaction receipts, bucket balances, and withdrawals. It also shows network and transaction states so a pending on-chain action is not presented as confirmed. The contract enforces a 30-day withdrawal cooldown for its savings bucket.

## Network and limitations

The documented application uses Ethereum Sepolia, a test network. BucketFlow is a demonstration of on-chain allocation logic, not a regulated savings product.

# Portfolio RAG Assistant — Portfolio questions and grounded answers

**Type:** Independent AI application project.

**Contribution:** Curated knowledge, Python ingestion and answering pipelines, evaluation tooling, and Gradio testing interfaces.

**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/portfolio

## Overview and contribution

Favour built the Portfolio RAG Assistant to answer visitor questions about his background, professional experience, contributions, and projects. He organized the portfolio knowledge into topic documents and implemented the Python pipelines that retrieve supporting passages and generate grounded answers. Relevant repository links direct visitors to deeper implementation explanations.

## Python implementation and retrieval

The Portfolio RAG Assistant uses Python, LangChain, OpenAI embeddings and chat models, Chroma, and Gradio. Its ingestion pipeline loads curated Markdown, extracts YAML metadata separately from searchable text, preserves document identity and section metadata, and creates deterministic heading-aware chunks. The local synchronization workflow upserts current chunks before deleting obsolete records.

The answering pipeline performs semantic retrieval and constructs a grounded answer from the retrieved passages. For conversation follow-ups, it rewrites the question into a standalone retrieval query while preserving the original question for answering. The documented configuration uses text-embedding-3-large for embeddings and gpt-4.1-mini for answering.

## Evaluation and testing interfaces

Favour implemented a 50-question evaluation dataset with reference answers, answerability labels, and document-and-section evidence groups. Retrieval metrics include mean reciprocal rank (MRR) and section-based evidence-group coverage. Structured answer judging scores accuracy, completeness, relevance, and grounding.

Gradio interfaces support chat with retrieved-passage inspection, single-case evaluation, and sequential batch evaluation with category charts and individual feedback. Offline tests check implementation behavior with storage and providers mocked; they do not establish real retrieval or generated-answer quality.

This knowledge entry does not supply a verified overall answer-accuracy
figure. A dataset, judge, metric implementation, or passing mocked test is
not a measured quality result and does not prove overall correctness.
No verified numeric quality figure is supplied here. A separate AI-assisted
assessment is AI-assisted evidence, not independent human validation or
production accuracy.

## Availability and limitations

Public availability through Favour's portfolio was confirmed by Favour on 11 November 2026. The approved code link is https://github.com/faelic/portfolio; public availability has not been independently verified by the corpus authoring process.

The assistant is bounded by its curated evidence. It does not automatically browse GitHub, and the corpus provides no measured retrieval-quality, production-scale, or uptime guarantees. The RAG implementation does not establish deployment of autonomous agents, model training, or fine-tuning.

# Approval Cleanup — ERC-20 wallet-permission manager

**Type:** Independent blockchain application  
**Also known as:** Cleanup; Allowance Cleanup.  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/approval-cleanup  
**Application:** https://approval-cleanup-brt3.vercel.app/  
**Stack:** Next.js, React, TypeScript, wagmi, viem, Hardhat, OpenZeppelin.

## Overview and contribution

Approval Cleanup helps wallet owners review ERC-20 token allowances granted to other addresses or contracts. Favour built the interface for scanning recent Approval events, identifying the latest observed token-and-spender allowances, and calling attention to permissions that deserve a closer look, including unlimited and older approvals.

Approval Cleanup scans a recent block window and cannot guarantee a complete history of every approval a wallet has ever granted.

## Log processing and wallet actions

Approval Cleanup retrieves logs in batches that work within RPC provider limits, then separates normalization and risk checks from the interface. Users can review an allowance and initiate an update or revocation through their connected wallet.

Approval Cleanup's scan covers a recent block window; provider constraints and non-standard tokens can affect the results.

## Coverage limitations

Because Approval Cleanup's scan covers a recent block window, it cannot guarantee a complete history of every approval a wallet has ever granted. Non-standard tokens and provider constraints can also affect what the application finds.

# Favour's engineering perspective and interests

The following passages express Favour Chukwuemerie Ututu's perspective, with owner-approved wording updates on 11 November 2026.

## Favour's engineering perspective — in his own words

I started my career as a frontend engineer, so I've always loved seeing beautiful user interfaces. But they have to work, too. I love an interface that looks good, feels easy to use, and loads quickly. I don't want to wait a minute for a page to load just to do something simple.

As I kept building, I got more curious about what happens beneath the interface. Security, especially, caught my attention. It could be frontend security, backend security, or AI security. I want to understand where things can go wrong, what makes a system vulnerable, and what it takes to protect it. That curiosity is also what got me interested in AI safety.

I value well-architected products and the engineers who build them. I have a lot of respect for engineers who would rather delay a release than compromise on security. For me, it's exciting to see a beautiful, functional interface sitting on top of a thoughtfully designed backend, with security taken seriously across the whole system.

That same thinking shapes how I approach AI safety and agent boundaries. I also care about the boundaries around it: what it can access, what actions it can take, what needs human approval, and how it behaves when something unexpected happens. I care about building systems that are useful without being careless about safety.

## Favour's interests — in his own words

I love coding. I enjoy working with LLMs, experimenting with what they can do, and exploring their potential in applications. I'm especially curious about what becomes possible as AI systems get better at using tools and handling more complex tasks.

And I love playing video games. I really do. It's one of my favourite things to do outside coding.

Favour's frontend examples include Policy.ng's public website and administrative tools, and BlockScan's live blockchain explorer. ## AI application engineering

Favour builds LLM-powered applications with Python. His Portfolio RAG Assistant connects visitor questions to curated portfolio knowledge, retrieves relevant passages, and generates concise answers grounded in those passages.

Favour implemented Markdown ingestion with YAML metadata extraction, heading-aware token-bounded chunking, embedding generation and vector storage, semantic retrieval, conversation-aware query rewriting, prompt and context construction, and grounded answering. The implementation uses LangChain, OpenAI embeddings and chat models, and Chroma.

**AI engineering:** Python, large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), document ingestion, YAML metadata, text chunking, embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, context construction, prompt engineering, grounded generation, and evaluation.

## Blockchain engineering

**Blockchain:** Solidity, Ethereum, Foundry, Hardhat, OpenZeppelin, wagmi, viem, Ethers.js, Alchemy SDK/RPC.
